method: Audited original summaries, body and reflections against professional guidance, peer-reviewed reviews/studies and NIH resources. SciSpace supplied discovery leads; source metadata and relevant claims were checked against accessible original pages. No app or question-bank edits. All replacement lessons are concise paraphrases, not quotations.

scispaceQueries.question: What do current clinical reviews and professional guidelines establish about anemia in chronic kidney disease, iron and vitamin B12 deficiency, inherited bleeding disorders, anticoagulant monitoring, and transfusion safety?
scispaceQueries.outcome: KDIGO 2026 lead independently verified at KDIGO and its complete guideline PDF; discovery result itself was not treated as full-text review.

scispaceQueries.question: What do clinical guidelines and reviews say about sodium and potassium disturbances, ionized versus total calcium, magnesium deficiency, phosphate shifts and intravenous fluid tonicity?
scispaceQueries.outcome: Returned results were largely cancer-, pediatric-, chapter- or other narrow-context sources; selected directly relevant NIH/journal originals through web research instead of treating broad matches as validation.

scispaceQueries.question: What evidence supports safe blood transfusion identification and monitoring, neutropenic infection recognition, heparin induced thrombocytopenia and bone marrow biopsy aftercare?
scispaceQueries.outcome: Preferred accessible original ASH/IDSA guidelines and blood-service professional guidance over poorly matched or unverified discovery results.

accessLimitations: Multiple PMC pages intermittently returned browser challenges. A full-text designation is used only when a successful open returned the article; otherwise evidence uses an actually inspected publisher or PubMed abstract.
NICE CG174 and NG239 full pages were blocked. Indexed extracts corroborated general concepts, but these are not counted as fully reviewed sources in the lesson evidence.

Bain bone-marrow complication studies were discovered but publisher/PMC/PubMed opens did not expose usable text. Accessible MedlinePlus and MSK aftercare guidance support the biopsy concept; no journal full-text review is claimed.

The WFH guideline PDF exceeded the web tool size limit, and PubMed exposed no usable abstract. The inherited-disorders lesson therefore uses two disease-specific NIH resources; the existing hereditary OpenStax section did not cover hemophilia.
Blood and immunity use professional society and NIH educational sources for basic physiology rather than forcing an unrelated treatment trial into the evidence.
replacements: Removed inaccessible Elsevier DIC e-library reference.
Replaced B12 textbook citation with NIH and directly relevant original clinical research; the opened textbook contains broader imprecisions not carried into lesson text.
Replaced incomplete hereditary-disorders reference coverage with disease-specific sickle-cell and bleeding-disorder resources.
importantQualifications: B12 neurologic disease can occur without anemia or macrocytosis.
CKD anemia is multifactorial, with relative EPO deficiency rather than a universal single-hormone cause.
UFH and LMWH monitoring differ; aPTT is not a universal heparin-monitoring test.
Potassium replacement needs controlled prescribed delivery and monitoring with renal function considered; no doses, rates or direct exam answer added.
Total calcium includes protein-bound, complexed and ionized fractions; albumin-adjustment formulas may misclassify status.
DKA may occur without marked hyperglycemia; total potassium depletion is common but kidney failure requires qualification.
Tonicity differs from bag osmolarity; dextrose in water supplies electrolyte-free water after normal glucose handling.
An elevated red-cell concentration does not always prove increased red-cell mass; thrombotic risk varies by cause.
classification: supported means original core claims were supported, even where clarity/source quality improved; qualified means a meaningful caveat or distinction was added. No lesson required a wholesale reversal.
limitations: This is a bounded educational evidence audit, not a systematic review or clinician sign-off. No claim of complete or 100% accuracy is made.
